items.title: Bob Haggart interviewed by Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, September 22, 1995
items.q: They say Glenn Miller was very good at that — that was one of the best things he did was be able to doctor up arrangements.

ctx.x: Do you feel the appreciation is greater, and if so why?

I guess it’s because they’ve gotten it through just recordings. And when you come over in person they’re very thrilled. And they have all these records and they want you to autograph the records and they come in with a pile of records like that, and a lot of this stuff came out in Europe and you didn’t even know they existed. Of course you never see any royalties, that’s for sure. Things come out. So you sign a whole bunch of these things and it’s really an ego trip because you didn’t realize that people cared,…
Is there anything we can do to kind of create that respect for this art form, right here in the United States?
